Flexbox

W3C CSS Snapshot 2026

Flexbox arranges a group of boxes in one direction at a time. The box with display: flex is the flex container. Its direct children are the flex items.

Open interactive lesson

On this page

  • Choose the direction of the main axis
  • Align items on each axis

  • Official references

Choose the direction of the main axis

The main axis is the direction items follow. flex-direction: row follows the horizontal writing direction in this example. column places items vertically. The cross axis goes across the main axis.

How to try it Save this example as a new .html file, then open it in your browser. After a change, save and reload.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Choose the direction of the main axis</title>
  <style>
    .cards { display: flex; flex-direction: row; gap: 12px; }
    .cards > div { background: #d6efea; padding: 8px; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="cards"><div>Pen</div><div>Notebook</div><div>Folder</div></div>
</body>
</html>

What to expect Three items appear in a row. Change row to column to stack them.

Align items on each axis

justify-content uses extra space along the main axis. align-items aligns items across it. With a row direction here, those are horizontal and vertical respectively.

How to try it Save this example as a new .html file, then open it in your browser. After a change, save and reload.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Align items on each axis</title>
  <style>
    .cards { display: flex; min-height: 100px; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; border: 2px solid; }
    .cards > div { background: #d6efea; padding: 8px; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="cards"><div>Pen</div><div>Notebook</div><div>Folder</div></div>
</body>
</html>

What to expect Items spread across the row and sit at the vertical center.

Wrap items when a row runs out of room

Flexbox uses one line by default. flex-wrap: wrap allows more lines. A flex item can get a starting size with flex-basis; here each uses 100px. gap separates items and the lines when they wrap.

How to try it Save this example as a new .html file, then open it in your browser. After a change, save and reload.

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Wrap items when a row runs out of room</title>
  <style>
    .cards { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; width: 240px; gap: 10px; }
    .cards > div { flex-basis: 100px; background: #d6efea; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="cards"><div>Pen</div><div>Notebook</div><div>Folder</div></div>
</body>
</html>

What to expect Pen and Notebook fit on line one. Folder moves to line two.
